newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Banque Paribas Suisse in the black after 1995 loss.
newsitem.headline: Banque Paribas Suisse in the black after 1995 loss.

text.p: Banque Paribas Suisse, the oldest foreign-owned private bank in Switzerland, reported net 1996 operating profits of 49.6 million Swiss francs on Thursday after a 1995 loss of 11.7 million.

The Geneva-based bank, with branches in Zurich, Lugano and Basle, also said its consolidated profits rose to 113.8 million Swiss francs from 10.3 million following a mid-1996 sale of a stake in Turkish Ottoman Bank to Garanti Bank for $245 million.
A spokesman for Paribas, which also offers commercial bank services, said 1995 operating profits was eaten up by write-offs on certain bad debts but gave no figure for existing soft loans.

Banque Paribas Suisse, established in Switzerland in 1872 and fully owned by Banque Paribas France, has 10 billion Swiss francs under management in private client assets, up 16 percent over 1995, a bank statement said.
